  • 09 Oct 09:45

    Friday, October 9, Azerbaijan. European Parliament urges Azerbaijan to free political prisoners; Milli Majlis calls resolution “biased”

    ● The European Parliament has adopted a resolution calling on the Azerbaijani authorities to stop persecuting critics, journalists, human rights defenders and the opposition, release political prisoners and drop the charges against them. The resolution specifically mentions Ali Karimli, chairman of the Azerbaijan Popular Front Party, and opposition politicians Anar Mammadli, who was sentenced to 13 years in prison, and Anar Abdullayev, who received a 12-year sentence. The resolution states that Azerbaijan has more than 300 political prisoners, including 19 Armenian citizens who have been convicted. The European Parliament said that any future partnership agreement with the European Union must include progress on human rights and the release of political prisoners.

    ● The Milli Majlis described the European Parliament’s resolution as a “biased political action” based on false and fabricated information, rejecting accusations of human rights violations and the existence of political prisoners in Azerbaijan. Azerbaijani MPs accused the European Parliament of applying a selective and discriminatory approach to human rights and pointed to problems within European countries themselves, including the excessive use of force by law enforcement agencies and restrictions on freedom of peaceful assembly. According to the Milli Majlis, restoring trust requires not declarative appeals but a genuine change in the European Parliament’s approach, an end to confrontational rhetoric and recognition of the equal status of interparliamentary relations.

    Context. On 1 May this year, the Milli Majlis decided to suspend cooperation with the European Parliament in all areas. This followed repeated references to Azerbaijan in a European Parliament resolution on supporting democracy in Armenia. The document also claimed that Azerbaijan was “illegally holding Armenian prisoners of war” and called for their immediate and unconditional release. Azerbaijan’s Foreign Ministry condemned these as “unfounded and biased statements”. In mid-September, President Ilham Aliyev described the European Parliament as a “breeding ground for corruption”.

    ● Representatives of Azerbaijan and Armenia held a technical meeting to discuss the construction of power lines as part of the TRIPP transit project from Azerbaijan through Armenia. Particular attention was reportedly paid to coordination between the relevant agencies.

    ● President Ilham Aliyev attended the eighth Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan in Turkmenbashi, Turkmenistan. Azerbaijan became a full member of this format in November 2025. In 2027, Azerbaijan will assume the chairmanship of the Consultative Meeting format for the first time, for a one-year term.

    ● Speaking at the forum, Ilham Aliyev highlighted the significant expansion of trade and economic cooperation, joint projects and regular reciprocal high-level visits.

    Last year, Azerbaijan’s trade turnover with Central Asian countries increased by more than 50 per cent.

    Joint investment funds have been established by Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, each with capital amounting to hundreds of millions of dollars.

    Ilham Aliyev identified transport routes connecting both shores of the Caspian Sea as a key area of cooperation. These include the Digital Silk Way project, which involves laying fibre-optic cables along the seabed of the Caspian Sea.

    Transit freight volumes along the Middle Corridor increased by more than 10 per cent last year and by almost another 20 per cent in the first eight months of this year.

    Oil from Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan is transported through Azerbaijan.

    Work is under way with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan to establish a green energy corridor.

    ● Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov proposed creating a unified electronic trading platform for Central Asia and Azerbaijan at the meeting. He also proposed combining the region’s tourism potential by establishing a Caspian route under the slogan “One journey – several countries”.

    ● Tajik President Emomali Rahmon proposed holding a Central Asia–Azerbaijan business forum in the city of Khiva in 2027. The forum would develop concrete ways to implement the formula “Six economies – one product”.

    ● Member states of the Organisation of Turkic States will create a unified map and catalogue of geographical names. The agreement was reached in Astana following the third meeting of the heads of cartographic institutions of the OTS member states.

    ● The Foreign Ministry issued a statement following mine explosions in the Jabrayil district, in which a father and son grazing livestock in an uncleared area sustained serious injuries. According to the ministry, 443 people have been affected by landmines in territories liberated from Armenian occupation since the end of the 2020 war. Azerbaijan is calling on the international community to pay greater attention to the country’s mine-clearance efforts, the statement said. The Azerbaijan National Agency for Mine Action (ANAMA), the Interior Ministry and the Prosecutor General’s Office once again urged citizens to observe safety rules.

    ● President Ilham Aliyev posted a message on X expressing hope that “the historic efforts of President Donald Trump to establish lasting peace in our region will receive due recognition in the awarding of this year’s Nobel Peace Prize”. Aliyev recalled that “Azerbaijan and Armenia jointly nominated President Trump on my initiative”.

    PHOTO: A visit to Aghdam in Karabakh by internationally renowned travellers from 13 countries has come to an end. The group members belong to the international Most Traveled People club. They visited the Aghdam Imaret complex.

  • 09 Oct 09:45

    Friday, October 9, Armenia. Nikol Pashinyan and Ilham Aliyev have informal conversation at CIS summit

    ● Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is attending a meeting of the CIS Council of Heads of State in Turkmenbashi, Turkmenistan. Footage has emerged on social media showing him engaged in an animated informal conversation with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev.

    ● Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan held a one-on-one meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Turkmenbashi. The discussions reportedly focused on developing bilateral trade and economic ties. The importance of establishing peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan and promoting regional cooperation was also emphasised.

    ● Nikol Pashinyan also met with the president of Turkmenistan.

    ● No exact dates have yet been set for Nikol Pashinyan’s upcoming visit to Russia, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said. Earlier, Vladimir Putin invited Pashinyan to visit Moscow to discuss specific issues of bilateral cooperation. The invitation followed their meeting on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.

    ● The extradition of Azerbaijani serviceman Nasimi Musayev, who illegally crossed into Armenia and injured a local woman, is not being discussed, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told journalists during his regular one-hour briefing. He also stressed that Baku had not made such a request. At the same time, he said that if Musayev had not committed a crime, Armenia would have returned him the same day. Read more here.

    ● Foreign Minister and Minister of International Trade Ararat Mirzoyan held a phone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi. They discussed progress in implementing agreements reached during Mirzoyan’s visit to Tehran earlier this week.

    ● A commission has been established in Armenia by decision of the prime minister to prevent the introduction and spread of plague from Russia’s Irkutsk region into Armenia.

    ● The Armenian authorities have approved a proposal to sign the Council of Europe Convention on the Co-production of Audiovisual Works in the Form of Series. The government said signing the convention would facilitate the participation of Armenian producers in international projects, expand opportunities for distributing Armenian television series on international markets and improve their competitiveness. Eleven Council of Europe member states have signed the convention so far: France, Georgia, Greece, Italy, Luxembourg, Malta, Montenegro, Poland, Portugal, Moldova and the United Kingdom.

    ● Armenian Culture Days in Georgia have begun in Tbilisi.

    ● A man wanted in connection with a murder in Yerevan has been detained in Georgia. The 37-year-old, identified as M. M., is accused of committing a firearm murder in February 2026 in Yerevan’s Ajapnyak administrative district. He also faces charges of hooliganism and illegal acquisition and possession of firearms and ammunition.

  • 09 Oct 09:45

    Friday, October 9, Georgia. The European Parliament has adopted a resolution condemning the attempt to ban opposition parties in Georgia

    ● The European Parliament has adopted a resolution condemning the attempt to ban opposition parties in Georgia. The document was supported by 445 MEPs, with 37 voting against and 97 abstaining. MEPs are once again calling for the release of people they consider political prisoners and for targeted sanctions against the leadership of the Georgian Dream party. Read more here.

    ● The Prosecutor’s Office has launched an investigation into alleged violence against activist Sergi Kancheli by police officers. The case is being investigated under the article on abuse of official powers. Kancheli claims that on 27 September, six police officers stopped him, took him to a cemetery, physically assaulted him, cut his face with a knife and threatened him with a gun. According to the activist, he was also coerced into sexual intercourse. The Prosecutor’s Office said all necessary investigative measures would be taken.

    ● The European Union still believes in Georgia’s European future, EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos said in a video address published by the EU Delegation to Georgia. Kos said she remained hopeful about Georgian citizens’ commitment to freedom, democracy and a European future.

    ● Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova praised the Georgian government’s foreign policy. She said Western countries were trying to draw Georgia into “dangerous adventures” against Russia, while Tbilisi was resisting this pressure. According to Zakharova, Moscow understands Tbilisi’s efforts to limit external influence. She described the Georgian government’s position as a defence of national interests and sovereignty.

    ● An investigation is under way into the company Georgian Post. The Investigative Service has not specified when the investigation began or whether former company director general Levan Chikvaidze is involved. On 7 October, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said there were signs of corruption in the outsourcing of several Georgian Post services to intermediary companies.

    ● Danish brewing group Carlsberg has agreed to acquire PepsiCo’s production companies in Georgia and Armenia, Reuters reports. The company will acquire Iberia Refreshments in Georgia and JI Pepsi Cola Bottler Armenia in Armenia. The financial terms of the deal have not been disclosed, and its completion in Armenia requires government approval. According to BM.GE, PepsiCo’s production operations in Georgia, including Lay’s, Doritos and Cheetos, as well as local brands produced by Iberia Refreshments, will come under Carlsberg’s management. The company plans to establish a unified South Caucasus business cluster that will also include Azerbaijan.

    ● Georgia’s Prosecutor’s Office has charged 21 people with facilitating prostitution. According to the investigation, the accused opened massage parlours and hotels in Tbilisi, Marneuli and Kutaisi where sexual services were provided, keeping part of the proceeds for themselves. All 21 have been arrested. The offence is punishable by up to seven years in prison.

    ● An Armenian citizen wanted by Interpol under a Red Notice on charges of group murder has been arrested in Tbilisi. The arrest was carried out at the request of Armenian law enforcement authorities. The detainee is accused of group murder, hooliganism and illegal possession of firearms in Armenia. Legal procedures for his extradition to Armenia are under way.

    ● The assets of Georgia’s Pension Fund have exceeded 10.1 billion lari (approximately $3 billion). According to the fund, as of 30 September, 1,778,000 people were participating in the funded pension scheme. So far, 37,010 people have accessed their accumulated pension savings.

    ● Georgian-born doctor Shota Musaev has received an Israeli presidential award for civilian heroism. Musaev provided emergency medical assistance to a seriously injured pilot aboard a Flydubai flight and stopped the bleeding. On the plane travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, the co-pilot attacked the captain with a knife. Four passengers subdued the attacker, while Musaev, the only doctor among the 174 people on board, treated the injured pilot. The aircraft made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

    ● Georgian specialists may be involved in the restoration of one of the Georgian churches in Russia. Andria Jagmaidze, head of the Georgian Patriarchate’s public relations service, said dialogue on the matter had already begun. According to Jagmaidze, the church is not in Moscow. Its exact location and details of the restoration work remain unknown.

    ● Customs officers at the Red Bridge checkpoint on the Georgian-Azerbaijani border have discovered more than nine kilograms of undeclared silver and silver items. The goods were found during a detailed inspection of a truck driven by a Georgian citizen. The case has been referred to the Investigative Service of the Ministry of Finance.

  • 08 Oct 09:15

    Wednesday, October 8, Georgia. European Parliament draft resolution condemns attempt to ban opposition parties in Georgia

    ● A draft resolution prepared by the European Parliament strongly condemns the attempt to ban opposition parties in Georgia and calls for the withdrawal of the constitutional lawsuit. The document also reiterates calls for personal sanctions against billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili (founder of the ruling party, widely considered the country’s de facto ruler), Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili and Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze. The European Parliament will vote on the draft resolution this week.

    ● The EU Foreign Affairs Council will discuss Georgia next week. EU Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said this in the European Parliament in response to a question about the possibility of a broader suspension of Georgia’s visa-free regime and the introduction of targeted sanctions. Kos noted that the current developments in Georgia will be reflected in the European Commission’s enlargement report.

    ● Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze called Bidzina Ivanishvili the leader of the ruling team and the country, and said he plays a decisive role in ensuring the country’s security, peace and development. Kobakhidze also highlighted Ivanishvili’s key role in combating corruption at the highest levels of government. He made these statements in response to critical messages from convicted former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili. According to Kobakhidze, over the past year and a half, the highest levels of government have “in principle, been freed” of corruption.

    ● Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mikhail Kalugin said the EU is pushing Georgia towards “destructive confrontation” with Russia and putting pressure on Tbilisi to join anti-Russian sanctions. According to Kalugin, Georgia’s economic ties with Russia are “natural”. He also said that the initiative to restore diplomatic relations between Russia and Georgia should come from Tbilisi.

    ● Activist Sergi Kancheli has accused police officers of physical violence, threatening him with a weapon and attempting sexual assault. According to him, on 27 September, six police officers stopped him while he was out running, took him to a cemetery and abused him for about 50 minutes. Kancheli links the incident to his civic activism. The activist says he has left Georgia and is currently in a safe country. He says he has already filed a lawsuit against the alleged attackers.

    ● The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA) reports coercion against the lawyer of jailed Giorgi Davitadze, who previously stated that prison guards had raped him in prison. According to GYLA, the lawyer was detained for several hours inside the prison and forced to withdraw recordings he had made during a meeting with Davitadze. Convicted opposition politician Aleko Elisashvili said Davitadze’s case was accompanied by a large-scale protest in the prison, and several inmates injured themselves. The Penitentiary Service denies any acts of violence against Davitadze. GYLA is demanding an investigation and an immediate response from the Public Defender.

    ● The UN Human Rights Council in Geneva adopted by consensus a resolution reaffirming support for Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and addressing the human rights situation in Abkhazia and the Tskhinvali region, occupied by Russia. The resolution calls for immediate and unhindered access to the occupied regions for the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and international monitoring mechanisms. Georgia has submitted this resolution to the UN Human Rights Council annually since 2017. More details here.

    ● Health Minister Mikheil Sarjveladze said around 35,000 families will no longer receive unemployment benefits following an assessment showing that their social conditions have improved. Around 80,000 families have been assessed so far. According to the minister, as a result of reviewing the social assistance database, the state expects to redirect several tens of millions of lari.

    ● The drug Givinostat for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy is already in Georgia, and its free distribution to patients will begin in the coming days. According to the government, negotiations have also been completed to purchase another drug, Vamorolon. The innovative drug Trikafta for the treatment of cystic fibrosis will also be added to the state programme. All three drugs will be provided to patients free of charge.

    ● Economy and Sustainable Development Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili has been appointed deputy prime minister.

    ● New airports in the cities of Mestia and Telavi will become operational in 2028, with each able to handle up to 50,000 passengers a year. There are also plans to increase Tbilisi Airport’s capacity to 10 million passengers and put a new runway into operation at Kutaisi Airport. The government also plans to purchase new locomotives, carriages and passenger trains.

    ● The Georgian Railway workforce has been reduced by 1,100 employees, resulting in annual savings of 25 million lari (around $10 million).

    ● In the second quarter of 2026, the number of visits to Georgia from Europe increased by 23.4%, from China by 16.7%, and from Central Asia by 3.1%, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said.

    ● The state will invest 31 million lari (around $12 million) in infrastructure at the Gudauri ski resort. New cable cars, ski routes and an artificial snowmaking system are planned.

    ● Georgia plans to bring in around 200,000 free doses of seasonal flu vaccine this year. According to the director of Iashvili Children’s Hospital, the composition of the vaccine has been completely updated this year. The number of flu cases in Georgia is expected to increase from November, with the peak expected in late December and early January. The optimal period for vaccination is late October and early November.

    ● A new correctional facility with capacity for 150 inmates will open in Rustavi. According to the Justice Ministry, construction is almost complete and the facility will begin receiving inmates in early 2027.

    ● At the World Judo Championships in Baku, Tato Grigalashvili won the gold medal in the under-81 kg category. In the final, he defeated Azerbaijani judoka Zelim Tskayev in extra time. The 26-year-old Grigalashvili became world champion for the fourth time. He previously won the title in 2022, 2023 and 2024, and reached the world championship final for the sixth consecutive time.

  • 08 Oct 09:15

    Wednesday, October 8, Azerbaijan. Azerbaijan’s Media Council calls Der Spiegel report on August Hanning part of anti-Azerbaijani campaign

    ● Turkey’s ruling AK Party spokesperson Ömer Çelik said that “some countries are trying to destabilise relations between Turkey and Azerbaijan”, while some groups and social media users in Turkey are mistakenly targeting Azerbaijan. Çelik said Ankara and Baku are bound by strong brotherly ties based on the principle of “One nation, two states”, and that the two countries’ leaders have a brotherly relationship. “At the same time, each country has its own domestic politics, and there may be different approaches to domestic affairs and foreign relations. When we have disagreements on any issue, as brotherly countries, we resolve them through dialogue and continue on our path together,” Çelik said. Here is an analysis of the situation

    ● Azerbaijan’s Media Council protested against a report by German magazine Der Spiegel that an investigation into former German Federal Intelligence Service chief August Hanning is linked to Azerbaijan. Hanning was arrested on 6 October on suspicion of espionage, offences involving state secrets and attempted high treason. German prosecutors have not publicly named any countries or intelligence services involved, but Der Spiegel reported that Azerbaijan was among them. The council called the report “dirty disinformation” aimed at damaging increasingly close Azerbaijan-Germany relations. More details on the Der Spiegel report here.

    ● Pro-government Azerbaijani outlet AnewZ also rejected Der Spiegel’s claims, saying it had learned from senior German sources that Azerbaijan is not involved in the investigation.

    ● Former German Marshall Fund of the United States adviser in Azerbaijan Mehriban Rahimli was given a 7.5-year suspended sentence with a four-year probation period. She is accused of money laundering, abuse of office and other offences over funds received from the fund that were allegedly not registered as grants. Rahimli denies the charges, saying she was paid a salary under a service contract for 18 years, with taxes paid on time. “Can you receive a grant every month for 18 years?” she said. Rahimli is one of nearly 20 civil society representatives prosecuted after Azerbaijan revived its NGO case involving cooperation with international donors in 2025. Ganja Regional Community Centre head Asaf Ahmadov was sentenced to eight years and Ubuntu Social Work Association initiative group head Zamin Zakiyev to 7.5 years. Others have received suspended sentences, while trials continue. All defendants deny wrongdoing.

    ● Azerbaijan-British intergovernmental commission approved a 2026–2027 action plan at a meeting in Baku, covering more than 60 measures across 10 areas.

    ● Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov highlighted the shrinking Caspian Sea and called for joint action on shared environmental challenges at a CIS foreign ministers’ meeting in Turkmenistan. He also said the meeting discussed steps to increase freight traffic along the Middle Corridor and develop a strategic green energy partnership between Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

    ● A consultation meeting of Central Asian and Azerbaijani foreign ministers was also held on the sidelines of the summit. The talks focused on transport and energy cooperation and environmental issues, including the Aral Sea, water resources and the continued decline in the Caspian Sea level.

    ● The UN Human Rights Council adopted an Azerbaijan-initiated resolution on the impact of landmines on the full enjoyment of human rights and assistance to victims. The resolution, co-sponsored by 70 countries, was adopted without a vote. Azerbaijan, one of the world’s most mine-contaminated countries, called for greater international support and sustainable funding for mine action and assistance to victims.

    ● Azerbaijan’s UN representative Shahriyar Hajiyev said Baku opposes the “politicisation of human rights” and interference in states’ internal affairs. He said 96,000 Azerbaijanis had returned to territories retaken after the conflict with Armenia, while more than 4,000 people remain missing from the first Karabakh war in the early 1990s. Hajiyev also said Azerbaijan had, in accordance with national law and its international obligations, brought to justice the military-political leaders of the former unrecognised Nagorno-Karabakh Republic whom Baku holds responsible for serious crimes.

    ● President Ilham Aliyev said 4,010 Azerbaijanis are registered as missing following what he described as more than 30 years of Armenian “military aggression”. He said the International Committee of the Red Cross had failed to produce results in searching for them and called on Armenia to provide information about their fate, burial sites and relevant archives. Aliyev also urged the UN and other international organisations to step up efforts to locate missing people and support their families.

    ● During a visit to Finland, Azerbaijani presidential representative Elchin Amirbayov held high-level meetings with officials from the presidential and prime ministerial administrations, the foreign and defence ministries, as well as the Finnish-Azerbaijani parliamentary friendship group. Talks focused on the Armenia-Azerbaijan normalisation process and Azerbaijan’s cooperation with the EU. Amirbayov said Baku still expects Armenia to take steps to remove a major obstacle to formally establishing peace, stressing that “de facto peace does not yet mean the end of the peace process”. Finnish officials expressed hope for the agreement to be signed soon. The talks also highlighted Azerbaijan’s role in Europe’s energy security, ties with Central Asia and development of the Middle Corridor.

    ● Czech Transport Minister Ivan Bednarik will visit Azerbaijan from 11–16 October as part of a wider Czech delegation tour of Central Asia and the South Caucasus. He will be accompanied by Czech business representatives, including companies implementing or launching regional projects under the EU’s Global Gateway strategy.

    ● Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said Azerbaijan’s gas contract provides Georgia with 20-year guarantees on supply volumes and favourable prices. He also highlighted direct electricity imports from Azerbaijan and agreements on the joint operation of the Baku-Tbilisi-Supsa oil pipeline and the Supsa oil terminal as strategically important for Georgia.

    ● The EU has supported Azerbaijan’s education sector since 2008, implementing 29 projects, EU Ambassador Mariana Kuyunjic said. She noted that the fourth Study in Europe education fair in Baku on 10–11 October will bring together a record 60 universities and national education agencies from 16 European countries.

    ● Azerbaijan’s Justice Ministry is introducing an AI-based property valuation tool for notaries. The system will allow citizens to receive an estimated current market value of property when preparing for a sale or purchase.

  • 08 Oct 09:15

    Wednesday, October 8, Armenia. Nikol Pashinyan: Case of Azerbaijani serviceman in Armenia is criminal, but opposition “is turning it into an act of sabotage and terrorism”

    ● Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan commented on the criminal case against an Azerbaijani serviceman who illegally crossed the border and entered Shaki village in Syunik Province, where he wounded a local woman. “There is no doubt that this is a criminal offence. The court will make a decision, and the sentence — at least part of it — should be served in Armenia,” Pashinyan said. He noted that Azerbaijan has also opened a criminal case over the incident.

    ● Nikol Pashinyan said the authorities had no certainty that the fugitive soldier was on Armenian territory, which is why they did not warn local residents in advance. “A mother’s instinct did not allow the woman to wait for the police to arrive, but if she had waited, perhaps nothing would have happened,” Pashinyan said. He assured that the Azerbaijani serviceman’s victim would receive all necessary assistance.

    ● Nikol Pashinyan accused the opposition of “losing its sense of proportion” and said that “they are turning a criminal incident into an act of sabotage and terrorism”. “Obviously, this serviceman had some kind of problem; he left his military unit without authorisation and ended up on Armenian territory. Davitadze later told a court that prison guards had sexually assaulted him. The Penitentiary Service denies the allegation.

    ● Bishop Giorgi Jamdeliani of Marneuli and Hujab demands the release of the full video footage, including audio, in the Giorgi Davitadze case. He said the public has the right to know what happened in the prison and that those responsible for possible crimes should not go unpunished. The bishop also called for an investigation into the circumstances of the prisoners’ protest and possible beatings.

    ● Tbilisi protesters Murtaz Zodelava, Lasha Beridze and Guri Zhvania, convicted in the “4 October case” over an attempt to seize the presidential palace, have requested plea deals. The Prosecutor’s Office said they confessed to the crime and expressed remorse. Zodelava and Beridze were each sentenced to seven years in prison, while Zhvania received a five-year sentence. The Prosecutor’s Office said the decision on the plea deals will be made public later.

    ● Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili has travelled to Tanzania with a parliamentary delegation to attend the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union. According to the press service, Papuashvili will address the general debate and hold bilateral meetings.

    ● Georgia’s football team drew 0–0 away to Northern Ireland in the Nations League. After four rounds, Georgia are bottom of Group 2 in League B. In November, the team will play their final two matches — against Hungary in Tbilisi and Ukraine in Slovakia. The final group standings will depend on these matches.

    Monday, October 5, Armenia. Pashinyan on continuing cooperation with EAEU; Medvedev says “Armenia could become a second Ukraine”

    ● Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Armenia remains committed to mutually beneficial cooperation within the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), led by Russia. “This cooperation is aimed at ensuring sustainable development across the region. Armenia is consistently promoting an agenda of peace, trade and transport infrastructure in the region,” Pashinyan said during an online session of the EAEU Intergovernmental Council. At the same time, he again raised the issue of Russia restricting imports of Armenian products. “No significant progress has been made in the negotiations, but we need to continue constructive dialogue,” Pashinyan said.

    ● Despite Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s latest statement that Armenia does not plan to leave the Eurasian Economic Union, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko used the same online meeting to warn Armenia against leaving the EAEU common market. “There is no need to rush to throw away something that is benefiting you today,” Lukashenko said. “Believe me, as an old president with almost 30 years in office, no one is waiting for us anywhere.”

    ● Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan will visit Iran today.

    ● The Armenian Foreign Ministry’s press secretary posted about the foreign minister’s planned visit to Iran, using an old Iranian flag that is highly sensitive in Tehran. The flag was used before the revolution and is now used at protests against Iranian embassies abroad. “Accidental? Bad. Because a senior diplomat should know these details. Deliberate? Very bad. It is precisely because of such details that the bar in our relations keeps getting lower and lower,” Arega Hovsepyan, an MP from the pro-Russian opposition Strong Armenia faction, wrote.

    ● Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev said that “Armenia could become a second Ukraine”. “The political course chosen by Armenia’s current leadership will lead to nothing good,” he said.

    ● Medvedev told Iranian state media that “some countries are trying to divide the countries of the South Caucasus and damage Russia’s relations with Armenia”. Speaking to Iranian state media, Medvedev said: “First, the Western world offered Georgia NATO membership. Nothing good came of it. Georgia never became a NATO member. Its current leadership understands that this was the wrong approach. All this led to a conflict. Now our relations with Armenia are being put to the test.”

    ● Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze does not believe the Trump Route (TRIPP), a transit route from Azerbaijan through Armenia, could pose a significant threat to the traditional international transit routes running through Georgia. He said freight traffic along the Middle Corridor has increased sevenfold since 2020, creating an objective need to diversify routes.

    ● Kobakhidze said Georgia should continue work on the delimitation and demarcation of its borders with Azerbaijan and Armenia. “We have friendly relations with both countries, and work on this issue will continue in a completely friendly manner,” he said.

    ● Narek Karapetyan, head of the pro-Russian opposition Strong Armenia parliamentary faction, said he had a productive meeting in Strasbourg with officials from the European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines and HealthCare (EDQM). They discussed a party programme aimed at reducing medicine prices in Armenia to levels closer to those in Georgia. “Very soon, we will come up with a very interesting solution that will allow every Armenian citizen to save hundreds of thousands of drams a year,” Karapetyan wrote.

    ● The Catholicos of All Armenians met with a senior adviser at the White House Office of Faith-Based and Neighbourhood Partnerships. No details of the meeting were released.

    Monday, October 5, Azerbaijan. Reactions to Ilham Aliyev’s keynote speech at ruling party congress

    ●  A video dedicated to Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev’s keynote speech at the eighth congress of the ruling Yeni Azerbaijan Party on 2 October has been posted on his social media accounts. It includes excerpts from his remarks on the importance of Azerbaijan’s victory in the 2020 Second Karabakh War and the liberation of territories that had been occupied by Armenia for more than 30 years. However, the main message is the importance of peace and justice. “There is no place for emotions in politics. If we had given in to emotions, we would probably have erected a third Victory Arch in the centre of Yerevan by now,” Aliyev says in the video. More on Aliyev’s speech, including his tough foreign policy statements, here.

    ●  A conference titled “From the Shusha Declaration to the Organization of Turkic States” was held in Baku at the weekend, with guests from Turkey, Uzbekistan and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. Representatives of Turkic states’ embassies, MPs and activists also took part. The forum focused on exchanging views on the shared historical and cultural values of the Turkic world. 3 October is observed as the International Day of Cooperation among Turkic States.

    ●  A private residential building under construction collapsed in the Bakhар settlement of Baku’s Surakhani district, killing one person and injuring another. An investigation has been launched.

    ●  Baku hosted the “Taste of Europe” culinary festival at the weekend, marking 30 years of partnership between the European Union and Azerbaijan. The festival was organised by the EU Delegation to Azerbaijan and opened by EU Ambassador Marijana Kujundžić. Representatives of the Belgian, French, German, Polish, Portuguese, Slovak, Spanish, Croatian, Austrian and Estonian embassies took part.

    ●  Azerbaijani judoka Ahmed Yusifov won the world championship in the 60kg category in Baku. He defeated Kazakhstan’s Sherzod Davlatov in the final.

    ●  Azerbaijan recorded its first win of the current UEFA Nations League season, beating Lithuania 1–0 in Baku. The result moved Azerbaijan to the top of the group with five points from three games.

    Monday, October 5, Georgia. Tbilisoba-2026

    ●  Prisoner Iakob Guledani was found dead at Prison No. 17 in Rustavi. According to the Special Penitentiary Service, his cellmate found him hanging in the toilet. An investigation has been launched. Guledani’s family doubts the suicide version and is demanding evidence that there were no signs of violence on his body. According to the penitentiary service, he had been in prison since 2023 and was due to be released in 2028.

    ●  Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze rejected claims by convicted prisoner Giorgi Davitadze that ten guards sexually assaulted him in a conflict de-escalation room at the prison. Kobakhidze said the allegations were false and that this was confirmed by CCTV footage. The Special Penitentiary Service also denies that any violence took place. Davitadze made the allegations during an appeal court hearing and said the incident had been captured by surveillance cameras.

    ●  A total of 1,136 voters, or 51.6% of the electorate, took part in by-elections held in four municipalities. According to preliminary results from the Central Election Commission, candidate No. 41 Nanuli Khinikadze received 96.74% of the vote in Tsalka, while candidate No. 41 Vazha Kheladze received 87.16% in Vani. Vote counting is continuing at other polling stations. CEC Chair Giorgi Kalandarishvili said no complaints had been filed with district election commissions. One complaint was registered at a polling station and concerned photo and video recording rules.

    ●  Tbilisi hosted the traditional pro-European “Saturday march” under the slogan “Georgia against [oligarch] Ivanishvili”. Participants carried Georgian and EU flags and chanted: “Down with Russia’s rotten empire!”

    ●  Convicted former president Mikheil Saakashvili wrote on social media that he apologises to the country for failing to put up stronger resistance to billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili coming to power. Saakashvili also called on the “healthy majority in society” to forgive one another and unite. Nika Gvaramia, leader of the opposition Coalition for Change, responded on social media that he saw no point in apologising for failing to prevent the mass vote for Ivanishvili in the 2012 parliamentary elections. Gvaramia said what matters more is what opposition supporters are doing today and their active participation in protest rallies.

    ●  Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili marked the anniversary of the events of 4 October 2025, when a group of protesters attempted to storm the presidential palace. “This is the day when they tried to overthrow Georgia and were themselves overthrown,” Papuashvili wrote. Dozens of activists have been arrested in the “4 October case”.

    ●  World-renowned opera singer Paata Burchuladze, who was convicted in the “4 October case”, released the “Declaration of the National Assembly” from prison, which activists published last year. It declares the Georgian Dream government illegitimate and calls for a “peaceful seizure of power”.

    ●  The dismembered bodies of businessman Mamuka Tsereteli’s former wife, Elena Tsereteli, and her 19-year-old daughter were found in Moscow. According to Russian media and the Moscow prosecutor’s office, Georgian citizen Teimuraz Gogiashvili, born in 1979, has been arrested in connection with the killings. Investigators say fragments of the woman’s body were found in an apartment in Moscow, while her daughter’s body was found in the suspect’s garage.

    ●  Tbilisi hosted the traditional Tbilisoba celebrations at the weekend, marking the capital’s birthday. The annual ceremony honouring Tbilisi’s 2026 honorary citizens was also held, with doctors, scientists, artists, journalists and athletes among those recognised. Mayor Kakha Kaladze presented symbolic keys to the city to 32 families.
